extracted.intended_audience: press release writers, PR/communications professionals, journalism students and media relations practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluating or composing press releases according to core journalistic newsworthiness criteria so they are likelier to be picked up by media outlets. Uses seven core news values with practical tactics for PR writers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: How recently did the event unfold? Critical in 24-hour news cycle. Press release must be tied to recent event. Stale news rarely covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Tie to current news cycle, anniversaries, awareness months; score timeliness 0-2 in the implicit rubric.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proximity
rubrics_metrics.description: Local stories gain more attention. Affects audience directly. "Hyper-local" angles increase pickup. Geographic relevance matters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Customize for regional outlets with local data; assess proximity relative to the target outlet (score 0-2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of people affected; Magnitude of effect; Reach of consequences; Severity for those affected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Quantify reach (X people affected); emphasize magnitude/severity when framing the release; score impact 0-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prominence
rubrics_metrics.description: Notable people, organizations, brands. Politicians, celebrities, athletes more newsworthy. Major institutions. Recognized brands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Include named experts, celebrities, or major institutions to increase pickup likelihood; score prominence 0-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: The Unusual / Novelty
rubrics_metrics.description: Strange, surprising, or unprecedented. Counter to expectations. "Man bites dog" phenomenon. First / largest / most distant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Lead with the surprise or novelty; highlight 'first', 'largest', or otherwise unique aspects; score unusual/novelty 0-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict
rubrics_metrics.description: Disputes; Opposing parties; Resolution arc; Legal, political, competitive. Tension creates story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Frame a press release around a challenge, dispute, or opposing forces and any resolution arc; score conflict element 0-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Interest
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotion-driven stories. Empathy, grief, admiration, joy. Personal narratives. Beyond facts and figures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical strategies: Include personal stories or emotional hooks to create empathy and narrative appeal; score human interest 0-2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implicit newsworthiness scoring rubric
rubrics_metrics.description: Score press release 0-2 on each: Timeliness; Proximity (for target outlet); Impact (size and severity); Prominence; Unusual angle; Conflict element; Human interest. Total: out of 14.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoring guidance: 12-14 = highly newsworthy; 8-11 = solidly newsworthy; 4-7 = marginal; 0-3 = probably won't get covered.
